exam.title: Numerical Mathematics I - Exam B
exam.subtitle: Iterative methods, interpolation, integration, least squares
exam.instructions: Complete all tasks thoroughly. Provide algorithms explicitly and perform error estimates. Permitted aids: non-programmable calculator.

exercises.title: Jacobi Method and Convergence
exercises.description:
Consider the linear system $Ax=b$ with
$A = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$, $b = \begin{pmatrix} 15 \\ 10 \\ 10 \end{pmatrix}$.

a) Set up the Jacobi iteration.
b) Justify convergence.
c) Perform two iterations with $x^{(0)} = (0,0,0)^T$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Split $A = D + L + U$
$D = \mathrm{diag}(4,4,3)$, $L+U$ contains off-diagonal entries.
Jacobi formula: $x^{(k+1)} = D^{-1}(b - (L+U)x^{(k)})$

Step 2: Component form
From the rows of $A$:
$x_1 = \frac{15 + x_2}{4}$
$x_2 = \frac{10 + x_1 + x_3}{4}$
$x_3 = \frac{10 + x_2}{3}$

Step 3: Convergence
$A$ is strictly diagonally dominant: $4>1$, $4>2$, $3>1$.
Therefore Jacobi converges (diagonal dominance criterion).

exercises.title: Quadratic Lagrange Interpolation
exercises.description:
Given data points $(0,1)$, $(1,3)$, $(2,2)$.

a) Determine the interpolation polynomial $p_2(x)$.
b) Compute $p_2(1.5)$.
solutionSteps:
Step 2: Interpolation polynomial
$p_2(x) = 1\cdot L_0(x) + 3\cdot L_1(x) + 2\cdot L_2(x)$
$= -1.5x^2 + 3.5x + 1$

exercises.title: Trapezoidal and Simpson's Rule
exercises.description:
Approximate $I = \int_0^1 \ln(1+x)\,dx$ with $n=2$ subintervals.

a) Trapezoidal rule
b) Simpson's rule
c) Compare with the exact value $I = 2\ln 2 - 1$.

exercises.title: Linear Regression (Least Squares)
exercises.description:
Given data points $(1,2.0)$, $(2,2.9)$, $(3,3.7)$, $(4,4.1)$.
Determine the best fit line $y = a + bx$.
solutionSteps:
Step 2: Slope
$b = \frac{n\sum xy - (\sum x)(\sum y)}{n\sum x^2 - (\sum x)^2}$
$= \frac{4\cdot35.3 - 10\cdot12.7}{4\cdot30 - 100} = 0.71$

exercises.title: Explicit Euler Method
exercises.description:
Solve numerically $y' = y - x^2 + 1$, $y(0)=0.5$ with step size $h=0.2$.

a) Compute $y(0.2)$ and $y(0.4)$ with Euler.
b) Compare with the exact solution $y(x) = (x+1)^2 - 0.5e^x$ at $x=0.4$.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Euler formula
$y_{n+1} = y_n + h f(x_n, y_n)$ with $f(x,y)=y-x^2+1$

Step 4: Exact value and error
$y(0.4) = (1.4)^2 - 0.5e^{0.4} \approx 1.2141$
Error: $|1.152 - 1.2141| \approx 0.0621$
